title: KV: fragmentation-aware reclamation and prioritized spill policy
author: Priya Menon
description: Motivation: In long-running nodes we observed slow memory growth and suboptimal eviction choices caused by fragmentation and size-skewed items. This PR implements a fragmentation-aware reclamation strategy plus a prioritized spill policy to reduce tail latency when the KV cache needs to free pages. Summary of changes: 1) Add a lightweight arena fragmentation estimator that tracks free-run histograms per arena and exposes a fragmentation_score metric used by the reclaim path. 2) Implement a cooperative defragmenter that runs in small time-sliced windows on an IO-worker thread to coalesce free extents without blocking allocation hot paths. 3) Replace the single FIFO spill queue with a priority spill queue that orders candidates by a combined LRU-weight and size_score so that small high-hit items are preferred to remain in-memory while large cold objects are spilled first. 4) Introduce reclaim hints to the kernel selection logic so allocations for short-lived KV entries favor compact arenas, reducing cross-arena fragmentation. 5) Add telemetry: fragmentation_score, spill_priority_distribution, defrag_duration_buckets, and eviction_jank_rate. Backwards compatibility: on-by-default behind feature-flag "kv_frag_reclaim_v2"; existing customers continue on current algorithm until opt-in. Checklist: - [x] Fragmentation estimator + metrics - [x] Cooperative defragmenter with bounded CPU budget - [x] Priority spill queue and policy - [x] Integration with kernel allocation hints - [x] Unit tests for allocator heuristics and spill ordering - [x] End-to-end perf canary run and dashboard entries How to validate: 1) Run bench/kv-reclaim with long-lived mixed-size workload (scripts/bench/kv_reclaim.sh) and observe reduced memory high-water and lower eviction_jank_rate. 2) Use perf-canary preset "kv-frag" to validate latency p95/p99 under steady-state traffic. Related: builds on ideas from ENG-1742 (arena compaction) and addresses incidents SUP-2145 (out-of-memory due to fragmentation).

patch_snippets: runtime/kv/allocator.h: added struct FragmentationStats { uint64_t free_runs; double fragmentation_score; };
runtime/kv/spill_queue.cc: priority pick: if (scoreA > scoreB) choose A; // score = hit_rate / log(size+1)
runtime/kv/defrag_worker.cc: defrag loop sleeps for 2ms slices and yields to allocator under contention
review_comments: Ethan Zhang: I like the histogram approach; please add an upper bound on estimator memory and avoid per-allocation atomics.
Priya Menon (author): switched estimator to per-thread scratch + periodic aggregation to reduce atomic pressure (see allocator.cc).
Lena Kovacs: can defrag windows trigger GC-like pauses on low-powered instances? Add a knob to reduce budget.
Priya Menon: added feature flag and per-node budget percentage (default 0.5%) with integration test in perf-canary.
Marcus Hale: CI flaky on macOS build target; reran and logs look clean. Approved pending addressing allocator_test timeout.
Priya Menon: increased test timeout and optimized test setup to use in-memory backing store; all tests passing locally.
release_notes: Improves KV cache memory behavior by introducing fragmentation-aware reclamation, a cooperative defragmenter, and prioritized spill policy. Expected to reduce memory high-water and eviction-induced tail latency. Feature disabled by default via feature flag kv_frag_reclaim_v2.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature flag with caution: start at 0% rollout and monitor fragmentation_score and eviction_jank_rate.
If out-of-memory regressions appear, set kv_frag_reclaim_v2=false and restart node; changes are safe to toggle at runtime in canary builds.
changelog_entry: kv: fragmentation-aware reclamation + prioritized spill queue (feature-flagged) - reduces memory fragmentation and eviction tail latency
